question: Does the equal-|L|/free-direction competing-basin class track the truth tumbling regime (long-axis mode vs short-axis mode) or separatrix proximity (k^2)?
hypothesis: The multi-solution structure is regime-dependent; the equal-|L|/free-direction class concentrates on one tumbling mode rather than being seed-random or k^2-driven.
narrative_md: Re-scored s077's 640 basins stratified by truth tumbling regime. The equal-|L|/free-direction competing-basin class is almost entirely a long-axis-mode (LAM) phenomenon: 6 LAM seeds host 96/104 competing basins (median 14/seed), 4 SAM seeds host 8 (median 2.5). The distributions barely touch. Separatrix proximity is NOT the driver — the most near-separatrix seed (28, SAM, k^2=0.944) has zero competing basins. Ties the hard multi-solution degeneracy to an a-priori-knowable property. Medium confidence: n=10, loose surrogate gate. Uses truth state/regime -> oracle_clean false.
